walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme A: Relationships & Families — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme A: Relationships & Families brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme A: Relationships & Families.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: The Buddha created the universe.

No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
The Buddha created the universe.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
